messages:
marina_ml: FYI i'm starting onboarding for Thimble-12B (TinyOak release). license on HF repo is messy, looks like a non-commercial + no-derivatives clause mixed in. ran a quick 4-bit quant experiment, small regression on convQA and codebench.
marina_ml: Questions: 1) can we host this model on Redwood hosted API? 2) can we offer quantized weights to Dedicated/private customers? 3) any special attribution text we must show?
marina_ml: cc @jon_legal @sam_engineering @nina_prod

jon_legal: thanks Marina — can you paste the exact license snippet here? quick read-through matters a lot (NC vs ND have very different impacts).

marina_ml: paste below:
```
"LICENSE: TinyOak-Shared-0.9. Terms: NonCommercial; NoDerivatives without prior written consent; must include attribution to TinyOak in any public demonstrations; redistribution of modified weights prohibited."
```

sam_engineering: quick technical note — our 4-bit quantized run produced ~1.8% drop on convQA F1, and a couple blue-team prompts show hallucinations increased slightly. nothing catastrophic but measurable.

jon_legal: okay. high-level: if license has NC (non-commercial) then offering a paid hosted API is likely a violation unless TinyOak grants a commercial license. if it also has a NoDerivatives (ND) clause, then creating and distributing transformed weights (eg quantized) likely counts as a derivative and you cannot redistribute those weights.

jon_legal: hosting behind our API is a grey area: providing model-as-a-service can be considered "public performance" not redistribution — but many NC licenses still forbid commercial exploitation. we shouldn't expose this model to customers under paid plans without explicit permission.

nina_prod: for product decisions: could we restrict Thimble to internal eval + free research sandbox only? we can gate it behind a "research" tier and block export/downloads in the Console.

jon_legal: that approach reduces some risk but doesn't fix NC for paid offerings. recommendation: 1) block weight export; 2) mark model as "restricted" in catalog with license metadata; 3) disallow Dedicated weight delivery and Private on-prem shipping unless legal gets a written commercial license from TinyOak.

liz_sre: from infra/security POV we can add a flag to model-catalog to prevent export and annotate with compliance notes. also can add automated UI banner for required attribution text.

marina_ml: is quantization considered a derivative? i.e. if we quantize for latency improvements, is that a modification that triggers ND?

jon_legal: short answer: probably yes. ND is broadly interpreted — transforming weights (including quantization, pruning) typically counts as creating a derivative. even format conversions can be risky. so do not distribute quantized weights.

sam_engineering: ok we can keep quantized variants internal for benchmarking but not hand them off. would recommending we provide only hosted endpoints that route to quantized runtime internally be acceptable from legal POV?

jon_legal: hosting quantized runtime internally and exposing API without distributing weights is safer, but because of NC we still need to verify whether offering that endpoint commercially is allowed. if it's a free-tier research sandbox (no paid access) it's more defensible.

jon_legal: next steps i propose:
- marina: add full license text & upstream contact info to the model onboarding ticket
- liz_sre: add "no-export" and "attribution-required" flags to the draft catalog entry
- nina_prod: draft a gating plan (internal eval + free sandbox only) and UI attribution copy
- legal: i'll draft a short email template to request commercial & redistribution clarifications from TinyOak

marina_ml: noted. i'll update the onboarding ticket with the full repo link and attach the eval logs showing the quant regression.

ops_bot: model-catalog draft created: https://internal.redwood/models/drafts/thimble-12b (status: restricted)

nina_prod: attribution copy draft: "Model: Thimble-12B — provided by TinyOak. Use subject to TinyOak license terms. Contact sales@tinyoak.example for commercial licensing."

jon_legal: looks good. legal will hold off on issuing any commercial approvals until we get written permission. if TinyOak is open to negotiation we can request a commercial license for Dedicated/private redistribution.

sam_engineering: for our evals we'll keep quantized runs internal and add a note to the repo: "Quantized artifacts are internal only per upstream license." will tag any eval plots with that.

marina_ml: thanks all — i'll block the model for Dedicated/private deliveries and set the hosted API to research-only until we hear back. marking this thread done for now. :white_check_mark:

liz_sre: adding a monitoring alert to flag any attempts to export weights from the catalogue UI.

jon_legal: i'll send the first outreach email today and paste the thread reply here when i do. :eyes:

marina_ml: :thumbsup:
